summary: The Gram matrix of the coordinates commutes with the irreducible representation, so it is scalar; the trace fixes the scalar to 1.

steps.claim: From the cut pair: W(full) is integrable on 𝖴∖G₁(𝔰) (h2) and is a Bessel function, in particular bounded measurable (a).

steps.lean:
have {i j} := (h2.eval_piLp i).mul_of_top_left ((a .full).memLp_top.eval_piLp j).star
  simp [Pi.mul_def] at this
steps.claim: Each product W(full)_i·conj(W(full)_j) is integrable (integrable times bounded).

steps.lean:
apply (B.irreducible (of _) fun s ↦ .symm ((commute_unitary_iff_star_right_conjugate (by simp)).2
    (ext fun i j ↦ .trans ?_ (identDistrib_orbitMeasure_comp (measurePreserving_conj_bessel
    mem_besselU besselS_le_normalizer_besselU (mem_unitriGroup_of_mem_floorGroup (toBesselH_mem s)))
    (measurePreserving_mul_left _ (embedH s)) ?_ ?_).integral_eq))
    ).elim fun c hc ↦
steps.claim: The Gram matrix 𝒢_{ij} = ∫ W_i conj(W_j) dμ commutes with rep(s) for every s ∈ U(κ): the entries of 𝒢·rep(s) and rep(s)·𝒢 agree because left multiplication by embedH(s) preserves the quotient measure (conjugation by embedH(s) ∈ 𝖲 preserves the Haar measure of 𝖴, identDistrib_orbitMeasure_comp) and W(embedH(s)y) = rep(s)W(y) — the two identities left open here (steps 5, 6); by irreducibility 𝒢 = c·1 for some c.

steps.lean:
congr($hc i j).symm.trans (by
      apply_fun trace at hc
      simp_all [← mul_conj', trace, integral_finsetSum, PiLp.norm_sq_eq_of_L2, ← ofReal_inj,
    lintegral_enorm_sq _ (a _).memLp_top, ← integral_complex_ofReal]) <;> generalize ⇑(B.W .full) =
    F at *
steps.claim: c = 1: the trace of 𝒢 is Σ_i ∫ |W_i|² dμ = ∫ ‖W(full)‖² dμ = |I| (lintegral_sq_full_eq), and the trace of c·1 is c|I|; so 𝒢_{ij} = δ_{ij}.
First open identity: the (i, j) entry of the product with rep(s) is the integral of the corresponding linear combination (linearity of the integral).

steps.lean:
repeat simp [smul_def, *, mulVec_eq_sum, mul_conj',
    ← Finset.sum_mul, ← mul_assoc, mul_comm, mul_right_comm _ (F _ i)]
steps.claim: Second open identity: after the substitution y ↦ embedH(s)y, W(full)(embedH(s)y) = rep(s)W(full)(y) (map_H) and expanding the matrix-vector products gives the same integrand.
